memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If you lend money to one of my people among you who is needy, do not treat it like a business deal; charge no interest. If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, return it by sunset, because that cloak is the only covering your neighbor has. What else can they sleep in? When they cry out to me, I will hear, for I am compassionate." - Exodus 22:25-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God shapes how His people handle money and the poor, and His concern is unmistakable: do not use another person's need as an opportunity for profit. When you lend to someone struggling, do not pile interest on their hardship. And if you take a poor man's cloak as security, give it back by nightfall — because that cloak is the only blanket he has to sleep under. God cares about whether a poor man stays warm at night.

Look at how tender God's attention is. He notices the small dignity of a person having something to sleep in. He hears the cry of the one shivering in the cold. And He gives the reason plainly: "I am compassionate." God's laws about money flow straight from His merciful heart. To Him, people always matter more than profit.

This challenges the way our world so often treats the vulnerable — as opportunities to be squeezed rather than neighbours to be helped. God calls His people to a radically different posture: generosity that lifts people up rather than lending that grinds them down. Jesus embodied this perfectly, giving freely to those who could never repay Him (Luke 6:35). As we handle our resources, may we reflect the compassionate God who cares whether the poor sleep warm tonight.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I treat those in need as neighbours to help or opportunities to profit?
How can I use my resources to lift others up rather than burden them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Compassionate Father, You care whether the poor sleep warm at night. Shape my heart and my hands to be generous, lifting up the needy rather than grinding them down. Amen.
